target_customer: Game studios, virtual production, animation and 3D teams with large binary repositories
problem: Perforce is costly and heavy to operate and Git handles large files poorly, so creative teams lack a modern, cloud-native version control system.
business_model: SaaS subscription per seat or usage for hosted version control
product_category: Version control, developer tools for games and creative industries

founders.name: Sasha Medvedovsky
education: MSc in Computer Science and MBA, Tel Aviv University, cum laude

founders.name: Egal Lazarev
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by a search result summarizing company and press pages; YC page lists only Medvedovsky.

competitors.name: Perforce
competitors.what: Dominant centralized version control for AAA game development
competitors.traction_then: widely used in AAA games per vendor and comparison sources

competitors.name: Git with Git LFS
competitors.what: Distributed version control with large file extension

competitors.name: Plastic SCM (later Unity Version Control)
competitors.what: Version control tuned for large binary assets, used by Unity teams

technical_complexity.rationale: A cloud-native version control system with large file support, partial checkouts and engine integrations is deep infrastructure for a tiny team.

defensibility.rationale: Repos hold a studio's whole history, creating switching costs; the technology is hard to copy but Epic's Lore (open source) arrived later as a free alternative.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Epic announced Lore, an open-source version control for large projects (80.lv); Diversion responded by hosting Lore and says Epic recommends it for Unreal.

market_need_then: Game studios complained about Perforce cost and operations and Git's trouble with large binaries; Diversion's own surveys and blogs cite this, which is vendor material.

identity.mascot_or_character: Sloth in an astronaut suit and a robotic sloth on its pages
identity.visual_style: clean modern layout with gradient imagery

branding.brand_signature: Sloth astronaut mascot on the website
branding.community_and_virality: Active developer content on dev.to, a survey of game devs, event sponsorships (Global Game Jam 2026) and a CG Pro partnership.

brand_strength.rationale: Distinct mascot and consistent developer-facing content with press in GamesBeat and 80 Level, but no evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Diversion has kept shipping and raised more funding, with a reported $4.5M round led by Konvoy in 2025 and about $12M in total per GamesBeat. A repeat founder with two exits targets a clear pain at Perforce, though Epic's Lore and Unity's tooling are credible competitors. No shutdown or acquisition found.
notes: The 2025 round is labeled seed+ by coverage, so stage is other. Dealroom (aggregator, single source) lists a $7.4M seed in June 2022 led by Secret Chord Ventures at $30M valuation; not verified by a second outlet, so not recorded as a round. Total $12M per GamesBeat (seen via search summary; direct fetch returned 403). Competitor sources are undated vendor pages, not dated near the batch.
